why: For W(3,q) the ambient is F_q^4, so |ambient| and 2^4 coincide and cannot be distinguished. W(5,q) has ambient F_q^6, so the two come apart: det(B') must be 64 if Pass 275's identification is real.

verification_W5_8.reason: W(5,8) has 37449 points; the point/line build exceeded the time budget. The det test needs only t=1,2, so this is left as a stated prediction.

verdict: INCONCLUSIVE -- and the reason matters. Under a 2x2 transfer assumption the two ranks give Tr(B')=55 and det(B')=883, which is neither 64 (=|F_2^6|) nor 16. But that assumption is NOT justified here: W(3,q) is a polar space of rank 2, whereas W(5,q) has rank 3, so its natural transfer matrix is plausibly 3x3 and would need three ranks to pin down. Fitting a 2x2 model to a rank-3 geometry makes det(B')=883 an artefact of misspecification, not a geometric invariant. So this does NOT refute Pass 275's det = |ambient| identification -- but it does NOT confirm it either. The honest state is that the decisive test remains OPEN, and doing it properly requires rank_2 W(5,8) (t=3), whose 37449-point build exceeded the compute budget here.
caveat_model_misspecification: W(3,q) has polar rank 2 and a 2x2 transfer matrix. W(5,q) has polar rank 3, so a 3x3 transfer matrix is the natural expectation and THREE ranks would be needed to determine it. The det extracted here from two ranks is therefore not trustworthy as a geometric invariant. What IS solid is the new rank data below.

solid_new_data.note: first computation of the W(5,q) point/isotropic-line F2 incidence ranks in this program

reading: This is the experiment Pass 275 named as the decisive one. The transfer invariants are read off from just two ranks (t=1 and t=2), so the test needs no assumptions beyond the transfer form itself, and it can refute a claim this program has been building on.
